moat_against: Mid-single-digit share of a fragmented aftermarket; no pricing dominance
NA Automotive EBITDA margin ~7-8% vs >20% at O'Reilly/AutoZone
Competition from O'Reilly, AutoZone, Advance, RockAuto and Amazon
Large independently-owned store base limits control
EV adoption reduces moving-parts count over time
Planned Automotive/Industrial separation adds execution and dis-synergy risk
moat_for: Distribution density: ~10,840 locations and ~190 distribution centers near professional demand
NAPA brand and long supplier relationships in automotive aftermarket
Gross margin expanded every year 2021-2025 (35.2% to 36.8%)
moat_justification: Narrow/moderate moat: distribution density (~10,840 locations, ~190 DCs) serving time-sensitive professional installers, NAPA brand, supplier scale, and Motion's industrial service position; gross margin expanded 35.2% (2021) to 36.8% (2025). Against: mid-single-digit share of a fragmented aftermarket, North America Automotive EBITDA margin ~7-8% vs >20% at best peers, O'Reilly/AutoZone/Advance/RockAuto/Amazon competition, many independently owned stores, EV parts-count headwind, and no filed ROIC series in fundamentals.json past 2018 (20.6%/12.1%/17.2% for 2016-2018) to support a wide-moat claim.
name: Genuine Parts Company
one_liner: Quality narrow-moat distributor (moat 5/10) in a charge-heavy separation year — at $134.63 it yields only 6.8% weighted IRR vs IV@15% of $45.52; it clears 15% only below ~$46.
